_comment: Spelling hints and two small enums for pigeonhole.triage — NOT a gate. The old
closed-vocabulary boundary retired with unsupervised filing (2026-07-31): a human
tap now sits between the model and the filesystem, and path safety lives in
valid_segment()/under_docs() in pigeonhole.lib.sh.
THIS COMMITTED FILE IS A GENERIC SAMPLE. The values this box actually classifies
against live OFF the repo, at $DOCS/.pigeonhole.vocab.json, and pigeonhole.lib.sh
prefers that file when it is readable. The split exists because the live file is
harvested from a real corpus: doc_type and qualifier accumulate the clinics,
employers, insurers and addresses a person actually deals with, and owner names
real people. Published together those read as a personal profile rather than a
schema, which is exactly what happened — this repo is public and carried one for
about a year. Keep it that way: add real values to the local file, never here.
What each key is for: doc_type and qualifier are shown to the classifier as values
already in use, so the same vendor is spelled the same way across years — the model
may still coin a new one. owner is a real enum in the schema. _lookalike_families
routes notifications: a doc_type or folder listed there gets its own Needs-a-look
message instead of riding in the batch, so approve-all never covers it.
There is no folder list here: the prompt reads the live folders from disk.
The local file may additionally carry self_label, self_email and owner_identities.
Absent them the prompt degrades to owner=unknown -> needs_human=true for anyone
but the owner, which is the safe direction and costs nothing off-box.
Earned from a corpus's own history: a category listed here got mis-sorted before,
so it is never allowed to ride in an approve-all batch. A classifier will not beat
a careful human on the cases that already beat one.
Empty in the committed sample; the live file carries the real families.
